title: Rizia/Turn 10/STRIKE SCENE/HOUSE STRIKE FAIL/Revolution Fail Branch/Revolution Fail Branch Conversation

3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The heavy double doors crashed open, and a group of armed men rushed in.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: I quickly took cover. Everything happened so fast, it was difficult to discern what was going on, but I was sure Adarfo's men had the upper hand.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Instead of being overwhelmed, they unleashed a hail of bullets on the attackers.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: One of the guardians fell in the initial clash, but the others responded with unrelenting efficiency.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: In a matter of seconds, two of the attackers dropped to the floor.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: As the assailants began to fall back into the main hall, it became clear that the uprising was faltering.

10.speaker: Titus Gordion
10.text: "Now's our chance! Close ranks and move forward! Nobody leaves the library."

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: In rapid succession, two more attackers fell to Titus's marksmanship.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Titus motioned for his men to push ahead into the next room, but he stayed behind, keeping a watchful eye on me.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: He squeezed the trigger with lightning speed, dropping the would-be shooter before a single shot could be fired.

18.speaker: Titus Gordion
18.text: "Your pathetic attempt to use violence to force reform has been crushed."

19.speaker: Titus Gordion
19.text: "Your pathetic little rebellion has ended in failure."

20.speaker: Titus Gordion
20.text: "Lucky for us, we caught wind of it just in time."

25.speaker: Titus Gordion
25.text: "If you think everyone’s as corruptible as you... think again."

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: The pain was blinding, and my vision blurred as consciousness slipped in and out.

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: The Golden Guard seized me by the arms and dragged me into the adjoining room.

31.speaker: Player_Romus
31.text: "Name your price, Titus. Whatever you want -- money, power -- it’s yours. Just let me go."

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: I didn't have to wait long. A spray of bullets hit the ground near Titus’s feet, sending him diving for cover.

33.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
33.text: Use the element of surprise and make a run for it immediately.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: That was when I seized the opportunity and bolted for the door.

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: Just as I reached the main hall, a gunshot cracked from behind. A sharp pain tore through my left side, and I crumpled to the floor.

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: I looked down, blood pooling around my hand as I clutched the wound. Somehow, I knew it was Titus.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: I couldn't tell how much time had passed before the gunfire faded into silence. When my eyes focused again, Titus was standing over me.

42.speaker: Player_Romus
42.text: "Congratulations, Titus. You passed the test. Now, if you'll excuse me... I'll be going now."

43.speaker: Titus Gordion
43.text: "Take one more step, and I will restrain you."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Minutes seemed like hours, and before long, the gunfire subsided. Captain Castellanus approached Titus.

48.speaker: Player_Romus
48.text: "What? You believe I'd cooperate with these thugs?"

49.speaker: Player_Romus
49.text: "By what right do you dare to arrest me?"

50.speaker: Titus Gordion
50.text: "Right is defined by the oath I swore -- to defend the Crown's true purpose, not the whims of a single monarch."

51.speaker: Titus Gordion
51.text: "By the authority vested in me, I hereby declare King Romus is to be taken into custody for treason against the Crown."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: Titus, seemingly always a step ahead, reacted with calculated ferocity. As one man leveled a gun at Hugo, Titus' hand was already moving.

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: They were being led by Adarfo.

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: Minutes seemed like hours, and before long, the gunfire subsided. Titus turned to me after receiving the "all clear" from his men.

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: I didn't have to wait long. A spray of bullets hit the ground near Titus’s feet, sending him running in my direction.

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: My hand brushed against a bronze plaque that had fallen from its mount.

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: I grabbed it without hesitation and slammed it into Titus’s side, aiming for his kidney.

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: He grunted in pain, clutching his side as he doubling over as the blow landed.

67.speaker: Narrator
67.text: I didn't wait for him to recover. I scrambled to my feet and bolted for the main hall.

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: Several Wruhec's Guardians seized me by the arms and dragged me into the adjoining room.

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: As I was escorted toward the exit, I saw Vina and Mother watching from a distance with shock written across their faces.

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: As I was escorted toward the exit, I saw Mother watching from a distance with shock written across her face.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: I wondered if this would be the last time I’d ever see them again.

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: I wondered if this would be the last time I’d ever see her again.

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: I found a chair and sank into it, exhausted, as the muffled clamor of the uprising continued outside.

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: He turned back to his men.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: Hugo found his way to me.

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: Having Titus nearby would prove difficult, but not impossible.

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Adarfo was nowhere to be seen.

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: Especially since I knew his weak spot.

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: Adarfo proudly stood, raising his arms high.

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: But to my dismay, I soon came to realize that the Golden Guard was far from the vulnerable targets I had anticipated.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: Adarfo and his revolutionaries flooded in like an unstoppable tide, and the room erupted in gunfire.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: One guardsman fell in the initial clash, but the others responded with unrelenting efficiency.

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: As his revolutionaries flooded in like an unstoppable tide, Adarfo joined the fray, and the room erupted in gunfire.

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: But to my dismay, I soon came to realize that the Wruhec's Guardians were far from the vulnerable targets I had anticipated.

116.speaker: Lucita Azaro
116.text: "Romus... tell me you didn't have anything to do with this."

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: Lucita found her way to me.

118.speaker: Player_Romus
118.text: "There's no time for this. I have to make sure my mother and Vina are safe."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "I don't know what you are talking about."

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: "Quiet, woman! I don't need your meddling right now!"

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "You may not see it now, but believe me when I say that I was doing what was best for the country -- for us."

122.speaker: Lucita Azaro
122.text: "What the hell... Do you have any idea what you've done?! You've ruined everything!"

126.speaker: Lucita Azaro
126.text: "How dare you speak to me with such disrespect! Answer me now! Were you or were you not involved?"

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "I’m sorry. I made a mistake. I never meant for it to come to this."

128.speaker: Lucita Azaro
128.text: "What?! Do you have any idea what you've done? You've ruined everything!"

129.speaker: Lucita Azaro
129.text: "You're lying! I can see it in your eyes! Your delusions have ruined our child's life..."

130.speaker: Lucita Azaro
130.text: "Your mother?! What about our child? Admit it, Romus, you've ruined everything."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "Ruined? We've been heading down this path for a long time."

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "I'll speak to you any way I damn well please! I don't have to explain myself to you or anyone else!"

134.speaker: Player_Romus
134.text: "No, I wasn’t! And I won’t stand here and be accused of such treachery!"

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "Alright! I admit it! I was behind it from the start! I wanted to tear down the monarchy brick by brick! There. Is that what you wanted to hear?"

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: My eyes met Lucita’s, her expression filled with scorn and hatred.

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "Don't worry. We'll find a way out of this."

140.speaker: Lucita Azaro
140.text: "'Sorry' isn't going to cut it. What you've done is unforgivable."

141.speaker: Lucita Azaro
141.text: "You’re naive if you think there’s any way out of this now."

142.speaker: Lucita Azaro
142.text: "If we’ve been heading down this path, it’s because you refused to see the signs along the way."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: I turned away, my gaze falling on Hugo. His expression mirrored Lucita’s, filled with contempt.

144.speaker: Hugo Toras
144.text: "Your Majesty... tell me you didn't have anything to do with this."

148.speaker: Hugo Toras
148.text: "You yourself compromised their safety, didn't you? My God, Romus... You've ruined everything."

152.speaker: Hugo Toras
152.text: "I wish I could believe you didn't wish to bring ruin on this kingdom, Romus. I really do..."

158.speaker: Hugo Toras
158.text: "So it is true! Dear God, Romus... Do you have any idea what you've done? You've ruined everything!"

163.speaker: Hugo Toras
163.text: "Then it's true? Dear God, Romus... Do you have any idea what you've done? You've ruined everything!"

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "You may not see it now, but believe me when I say that I was doing what was best for the country -- for the family."

166.speaker: Player_Romus
166.text: "Hold your tongue, old man! I don't need your meddling right now!"

167.speaker: Hugo Toras
167.text: "'Old man?' How dare you speak to me with such disrespect! Answer me now! Were you or were you not involved in this upheaval?"

171.speaker: Hugo Toras
171.text: "Apologies are meaningless. What you've done is unforgivable."

175.speaker: Hugo Toras
175.text: "You're a fool if you think there's any way out of this now."

179.speaker: Hugo Toras
179.text: "If we've been heading down this path, it's because you chose to ignore the signs along the way."

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: My eyes met Hugo's, his expression filled with contempt.

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: From the corner of my eye, I saw Lucita and motioned for her to follow. But seeing the guards around her, I realized she was trapped. I pressed on.

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: From the corner of my eye, I saw Lucita and motioned for her to follow. But seeing the guards around her, I realized she couldn't so I pressed on.

201.speaker: Player_Romus
201.text: "There's no time for this. I have to make sure my mother and the others are safe."

202.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
202.text: Wait for the right moment, then run.

204.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
204.text: Wait for him to come closer.

205.speaker: Narrator
205.text: He twisted away. The plaque connected with a spot on his side just above my intended target.

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: He coughed and took a few steps backwards.

208.speaker: Narrator
208.text: I didn't wait for him to recover. I scrambled to my feet and bolted for the main atrium.

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "I consent. Just don't hurt my family."

210.speaker: Player_Romus
210.text: "You fool. Adarfo was right. The Crown will crumble into insignificance, and the people will take power."

211.speaker: Titus Gordion
211.text: "Adarfo is dead. And the monarchy will live forever."

212.speaker: Titus Gordion
212.text: "Your family had nothing to do with this scheme. They will live."
